llm.summary: The skill's requests and runtime instructions are coherent with controlling a local macOS BLE vibrator, but it asks you to clone and run third‑party code that you should review before executing.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the instructions: the skill describes calling a local HTTP bridge that broadcasts BLE commands to a Venus/Cachito device on macOS. There are no unrelated credential or cloud access requests.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are limited to cloning a GitHub repo, running local Python scripts (uv run), sniffing the pairing ID, editing a local variable, granting Bluetooth permission, and calling a localhost HTTP API via curl. These actions are within the stated purpose, but they require executing third‑party code and granting Bluetooth access — review the linked server.py and ble_worker.py before running.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is instruction-only (no embedded code), but it instructs you to git clone https://github.com/AmandaClarke61/toybridge and run its Python code. Downloading and executing code from an external user repo is a moderate risk: the SKILL.md provides links to files to review, but there is no install spec or verified release. Verify the repository and confirm it does not perform unexpected network activity or run arbitrary commands before running it.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or credentials; it only needs local Bluetooth permission and access to bind a localhost port. Those requirements are proportional to controlling BLE hardware.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request 'always' inclusion or any elevated platform privileges. However, because the agent can autonomously invoke skills by default, enabling this skill could allow automated commands to the local device (vibration control). Consider whether you want autonomous runs to be able to trigger the toy without explicit user confirmation.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with its stated purpose, but exercise caution because it tells you to clone and run a third‑party GitHub project. Before installing/running anything: 1) manually inspect server.py and ble_worker.py (and any dependency installation steps) to confirm there are no external network calls, credential exfiltration, or arbitrary shell execution; 2) run the bridge in an isolated environment (VM or disposable mac) if possible; 3) confirm the server truly binds only to localhost and that Docker vs. native host addressing is configured correctly; 4) be mindful that autonomous agent invocation could trigger the vibrator without immediate user action — disable autonomous invocation or require confirmation if you’re uncomfortable; 5) keep backups and revoke Bluetooth permissions if you stop using the bridge. If you want, provide the repo contents and I can highlight any suspicious code patterns in server.py or ble_worker.py.
